title: Pangolin Tunnel (newt / gerbil / traefik)
description: The Pangolin ingress path end to end: newt (in-cluster connector), gerbil (WireGuard server on the VPS) and Traefik (public edge on the VPS). Companion to the Cloudflare Tunnels dashboard -- Pangolin carries the hostnames that cannot go through Cloudflare, chiefly Immich, which is capped at 100 MB per upload there.

panels.title: Tunnel — newt connector (in-cluster)
panels.description: Cluster-side view of the Pangolin tunnel. This is the only half that keeps reporting if the VPS becomes unreachable.

panels.title: Control Channel
panels.description: newt's websocket to the Pangolin server. This -- NOT newt_site_online -- is the liveness signal: newt_site_online{site_id="self"} reads 0 even while the tunnel is passing traffic normally, in every build (its setter has no callers upstream), so that metric is deliberately unused here. DOWN here does not necessarily mean traffic has stopped YET -- the WireGuard data plane can keep forwarding on the established session for some period after the control channel drops -- but HOW LONG is unknown. This tile did go red about ten minutes before the hostnames went dark on 2026-08-22, and that figure was once written down as the grace period; it is not supportable. The same incident deleted the A record every Pangolin hostname CNAMEs onto, and those records carry a 300s TTL, so resolver caches were expiring on a separate clock at the same time. Two countdowns, one observation, mechanism never isolated -- the real grace period may be far shorter. Measuring it would mean leaving DNS alone and blocking newt's egress to the VPS on 443/tcp while leaving 21820/udp open, then timing how long traffic keeps flowing. Until then, treat DOWN as an outage already in progress, not a warning.

panels.title: Tunnel Sessions
panels.description: Active WireGuard tunnel sessions held by newt. The series DISAPPEARS rather than reporting zero when no session is live, so `or vector(0)` keeps the tile showing 0 instead of a misleading "No data".

panels.title: Active Proxy Connections
panels.description: In-flight forwarded connections -- the closest analogue to cloudflared's "Concurrent Requests".

panels.title: Tunnel Latency (p95)
panels.description: 95th percentile WireGuard round-trip as measured by newt itself.

panels.title: Async Backlog
panels.description: Bytes newt has accepted but not yet flushed. Sustained growth means the tunnel is not draining as fast as the origin is filling it.

panels.title: Newt Version
panels.description: Running connector build. Aggregated on `version` because a range query spanning a pod restart returns one series per pod, and a stat panel draws a tile for each -- which rendered the version twice after a redeploy.

panels.title: Upload Path — Internet → Cluster (ingress)
panels.description: Immich mobile backups travel in this direction, and lifting the 100 MB Cloudflare upload cap is the reason the Pangolin path exists at all. Traffic INTO the cluster consumes the WAN's DOWNLOAD capacity -- measured at 258 Mbit on 2026-07-31 -- which is the dashed ceiling drawn here. Note the direction label is newt's own perspective: `ingress` is inbound to the cluster, i.e. user uploads.

panels.title: Tunnel Throughput (both directions)
panels.description: `egress` is cluster → internet (users viewing photos, bounded by the ~135 Mbit WAN upload); `ingress` is internet → cluster (uploads). Verified empirically: 25 HTTP GETs produced ~18 kB egress against ~3 kB ingress, confirming egress carries the responses.

panels.title: Tunnel Latency percentiles
panels.description: p50 / p95 / p99 of the WireGuard round-trip.

panels.title: Proxy Connections by protocol
panels.description: Active forwarded connections split by protocol. The otel_scope_* labels newt attaches to every series are aggregated away here -- left in, they make every legend entry unreadable.

panels.title: Connection & Registration Events
panels.description: Tunnel re-establishment activity -- the analogue of cloudflared's "Config Updates" panel. A steady non-zero rate means the connector is flapping.

panels.title: Control-Channel Messages
panels.description: WebSocket traffic to the Pangolin server, excluding ping/pong keepalives so real control activity is visible.

panels.title: Edge HTTP — Traefik (Pangolin VPS)
panels.description: Per-hostname request and status-code view. newt sees only opaque tunnel bytes keyed by tunnel_id, so this is the ONLY source that can say which app was hit and how it answered.

panels.title: Requests by Hostname
panels.description: Request rate per Pangolin resource.

panels.title: Responses by Status Code
panels.description: Direct analogue of the cloudflared dashboard's "Response By Code" panel.

panels.title: Errors by Hostname (4xx / 5xx)
panels.description: Non-success responses only. A 502 here with the tunnel panel healthy means the origin (Envoy or the app) refused, not the tunnel.

panels.title: Request Duration p95 by Service
panels.description: Time Traefik spent on the request, including the trip through the tunnel to the cluster origin. Service names are cleaned the same way hostnames are in the request panels, so the two read consistently.

panels.title: Open Connections by Entrypoint
panels.description: Concurrency at the VPS edge. `websecure` is public HTTPS; `metrics` is the tailnet-only exporter listener and should show roughly one connection per scrape.

panels.title: Edge Throughput
panels.description: Bytes across the public edge, as counted by Traefik.

panels.title: Let's Encrypt Certificate Expiry
panels.description: Traefik obtains its own LE certificates on the VPS, entirely separate from the cluster's cert-manager wildcard -- so cluster cert alerts say nothing about these. Days remaining per hostname.

panels.title: WireGuard — gerbil (Pangolin VPS)
panels.description: The transport underneath everything above. gerbil ships this exporter by default; it only needed publishing.

panels.title: WireGuard Interface
panels.description: Operational state of wg0 on the VPS.

panels.title: Configured Peers
panels.description: Every Newt connector and WireGuard client registered on the server. The cluster's connector is one of these.

panels.title: Proxy Mappings
panels.description: Active port mappings gerbil is relaying.

panels.title: Bandwidth Reporting
panels.description: gerbil reports per-peer usage back to the Pangolin API. A rising error rate means accounting is drifting even while traffic still flows.

panels.title: WireGuard Throughput
panels.description: Aggregated across peers deliberately: gerbil labels each series with the peer's WireGuard public key, which is unreadable in a legend and cannot be mapped back to a site from this exporter. Use the newt panels above for the cluster's own share.

panels.title: Relay UDP Packets
panels.description: Packets through gerbil's UDP relay, used when two peers cannot establish a direct path. Split by direction and type -- this metric has NO `result` label (unlike the other gerbil counters), so aggregating on one produces a single unlabelled series whose legend just reads "Value". The unit is a plain suffix rather than the built-in `pps`, which SI-rescales these small rates into unreadable "60 mp/s" milli-packets.

panels.title: Hole Punch Events
panels.description: NAT traversal attempts. Sustained `error` or `rate_limited` means peers are falling back to relaying instead of connecting directly.

panels.title: Management API Latency (p95)
panels.description: Pangolin → gerbil control calls. Slow peer operations here show up as slow site registration, not as slow traffic.
